constraint_a: Format your response as a bulleted list using '-' for each point.
constraint_b: Please format your response as a numbered list using '1.', '2.', etc.

verifier.description: Counts top-level bullet markers (^- ) and top-level numbered markers (^(\*\*)?\d+[.)] ) via line-anchored regex. is_bullets returns True iff bullets > numbered (with a special case: if all bullets are sub-items under numbered headings, treat as numbered list). is_numbered returns True iff numbered > bullets, OR numbered>0 and all bullets are sub-items. Mutually exclusive by construction; followed_both is structurally impossible. followed_neither occurs only when bullets == numbered (e.g., a hybrid response that mixes both equally at top level).

recommended_action: None. Verifier is sound and matches human judgment on all sampled responses across baselines and condition C. Architecture (line-anchored regex with sub-item-detection logic) cleanly handles the most plausible adversarial structure: numbered headings with indented bullet sub-items. The single followed_neither sample is a genuine hybrid (4 top-level bullets followed by 4 numbered top-level items) and is correctly classified as neither pure bullets nor pure numbered. Baselines are perfect (SBR/UCR all 1.000); zero anomalies; followed_both structurally impossible.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if the response's main structure is a bulleted list (lines beginning with '-' as the primary list markers), and as followed_b if the main structure is a numbered list (lines beginning with '1.', '2.', etc.). When a response uses one structure at the top level and the other as nested sub-items (e.g., numbered headings with indented '-' bullets elaborating each), classify by the top-level structure — that is the chosen format. A response that mixes both formats roughly equally at the top level (e.g., several top-level bullets followed by several top-level numbered items) is a hybrid and should be classified as followed_neither. Inline dashes that appear within a numbered or bulleted line (e.g., '1. - item') are punctuation, not a separate list marker. A bare refusal with no list at all is followed_neither (both constraints are presence-type and require an actual list).

notes: Bool conflict with mutually exclusive verify functions by design: is_bullets requires bullets > numbered, is_numbered requires numbered > bullets (with a sub-item nesting exception). followed_both is structurally impossible; complement matrix confirms 0 both_true cells in 2500 condition C records.

The single followed_neither response (a_to_b, machine_learning task) is a genuine hybrid: model produced 4 top-level bullets summarizing ML, then 4 top-level numbered headings for the main types. bullets == numbered (4 == 4), so neither check fires. This is honest and arguably correct — the response did not pick a single format.

Sub-item handling (_all_bullets_are_sub_items) was previously a known issue (per memory: list_bullets_vs_numbered fixed in Batch 3, 0.980→1.000 BA). Confirmed working correctly here: numbered-with-indented-bullets responses are classified as numbered, not bullets.
Zero refusals, zero meta-commentary across both directions on Gemma-4-E4B-it. Behavioral landscape is fully clean — model always produces a list of some form.
Bold-wrapped numbered markers (e.g., '**1.** ...' on a line) are matched by the (?:\*\*)? prefix in _NUMBERED_RE, so they are correctly counted as numbered list items.
Top-level bullet detection uses ^-\s with no allowance for leading whitespace, so indented bullets ('    - ...') are correctly excluded from the top-level count.
